EventName: China's NDRC releases the Iron and Steel Industry Development Policy
Rationale: First national steel capacity and consolidation policy, approved by the State Council in April 2005 and released by the NDRC on this date. Codifies the mill build-out behind the iron ore import growth of the period. No portfolio claim: the dry bulk basket holds one name until December 2007.

EventName: Vale settles 2008 iron ore fines at plus 65 percent
Rationale: First leg of the 2008 benchmark round, taken by POSCO, Nippon Steel, JFE and Kobe. Month-level only. The dry bulk basket holds three names, so no portfolio-level claim is made.

EventName: Australian miners settle 2008 iron ore at about plus 85 percent with a freight differential
Rationale: First benchmark to price a freight differential over Brazilian ore, which transfers part of the Capesize rate to the miner. Higher ore prices signal demand strength against a direct claim on freight economics. Month-level only.

EventName: Lehman Brothers files for Chapter 11
Rationale: Trade finance withdraws and letters of credit become unavailable, cutting cargo volumes. Against that, the collapse in crude prices opened the contango that made floating storage economic through the following two quarters, which is the same channel this table credits at EV020 and EV024.

EventName: Lehman Brothers files for Chapter 11
Rationale: Same credit channel with no storage offset, since dry cargoes are not stored afloat at scale. Charter defaults followed directly.

EventName: China announces RMB 4 trillion stimulus
Rationale: Investment-led package weighted to rail, road and construction, the demand channel for iron ore and coal. Announced on a Sunday; first tradable session is 2008-11-10.

EventName: Contango opens the floating storage trade
Rationale: Crude forward curve moves into contango deep enough to pay for a VLCC as storage, withdrawing tonnage from the spot market and tightening effective supply while cargo demand is falling. Window is approximate and quarter-bounded rather than event-dated.

EventName: Annual iron ore benchmark pricing is abandoned
Rationale: Vale, Rio Tinto and BHP move to quarterly index-linked pricing. Ore prices become volatile and responsive, so mill restocking behaviour and therefore Capesize demand become more variable within the year. The mechanism that set EV002 and EV003 no longer exists after this.

EventName: OPEC declines to cut production at its 166th Ordinary Meeting
Rationale: Ceiling held at 30.0 mb/d against falling prices. Sustained oversupply pushes crude into contango, making floating storage economic and withdrawing tonnage from the spot market. US Thanksgiving, so the first tradable session for the US-listed constituents is 2014-11-28.

EventName: OPEC declines to cut production at its 166th Ordinary Meeting
Rationale: Lower bunker cost reduces voyage expense, while the same price weakness signals slowing industrial demand.

EventName: US crude oil export ban repealed
Rationale: Section 101 of P.L. 114-113 removes the export restriction, opening a US Gulf to Asia crude trade that did not previously exist. A structural addition to average haul length that accrues over years rather than on the date.

EventName: Hanjin Shipping enters court receivership
Rationale: Largest shipping insolvency of the cycle, marking the withdrawal of European and Korean bank lending from shipping generally. Raises the cost and availability of capital for owners. Receivership granted 2016-09-01.

EventName: Hanjin Shipping enters court receivership
Rationale: Same financing channel, though tanker earnings were stronger at the time.

EventName: OPEC agrees its first production cut since 2008
Rationale: OPEC-14 target of 32.5 mb/d effective 2017-01-01. Less crude leaving the Gulf means fewer cargoes against an orderbook still delivering, which is the supply-side start of the 2017 and 2018 tanker downturn.

EventName: US withdraws from the JCPOA
Rationale: Reimposition of Iran sanctions removes NITC tonnage from the compliant charter market and forces Iranian barrels onto longer, less efficient routings. Snapback of oil sanctions followed on 2018-11-05.

EventName: Attack on Abqaiq and Khurais halts Saudi production
Rationale: Roughly 5.7 mb/d of Saudi processing capacity interrupted. Fewer cargoes in the immediate term against a step change in Gulf war-risk premium and insurance cost, which reprices the whole route. Saturday, so the first tradable session is 2019-09-16.

EventName: Refiners build compliant fuel stocks ahead of IMO 2020
Rationale: Refiners build compliant fuel inventory ahead of the sulphur cap while the COSCO designation removes tonnage, producing the largest tanker rate move of the decade. Window is quarter-bounded rather than event-dated.

EventName: OPEC plus cooperation collapses
Rationale: Russia refuses the proposed cut. Saudi Arabia discounts official selling prices on 2020-03-07 and commits to raising output around 2020-03-10, creating long-haul cargo demand and contango storage economics at once.

EventName: OPEC plus cooperation collapses
Rationale: Arrives with the first COVID demand shock and carries no offsetting cargo benefit.

EventName: WHO characterises COVID-19 as a pandemic
Rationale: Refined product demand destruction against a storage-driven rate spike running the other way.

EventName: WHO characterises COVID-19 as a pandemic
Rationale: Industrial shutdowns cut raw material demand with no storage offset.

EventName: WTI front-month settles below zero
Rationale: Storage scarcity at Cushing prices physical delivery below zero, which is the most extreme contango signal on record and makes floating storage economic at almost any freight rate.

EventName: OPEC plus agrees a record 9.7 mb/d production cut
Rationale: Effective 2020-05-01, tapering to 7.7 mb/d in July. Removes the cargo volume and collapses the contango that paid for floating storage, ending the storage trade and beginning the 2020 and 2021 tanker earnings collapse. The symmetric counterpart to EV015 and EV017. Announced on a Sunday.

EventName: China restricts Australian coal imports
Rationale: Unofficial ban redirects Australian coal to India and Europe while China sources from Indonesia, Russia and Colombia. Both legs lengthen, so tonne-mile demand rises even though tonnage is unchanged. Month-level; no single announcement exists. Relaxed from early 2023.

EventName: Chinese power rationing and coal price spike
Rationale: Provincial electricity rationing forces emergency thermal coal imports on top of an already congested global port system, producing the strongest Capesize and Panamax earnings since 2008. Month-bounded rather than event-dated.

EventName: Evergrande is declared in default
Rationale: Marks the start of the Chinese property downturn, which is the end demand for roughly a third of Chinese steel and therefore for seaborne iron ore.

EventName: OPEC plus accelerates the unwind of voluntary cuts
Rationale: Eight producers compress three monthly increments into one, adding 411 kb/d from May 2025 and beginning a sustained supply-addition phase that raises seaborne crude volumes.

EventName: Indonesia bans unprocessed mineral ore exports
Rationale: Removes short-haul nickel and bauxite cargoes to China, mostly Supramax and Panamax. Partly relaxed in 2017 and reimposed for nickel ore from 2020-01-01.

EventName: Fundao tailings dam fails at Samarco
Rationale: The Vale and BHP joint venture suspends operations. Brazil is the longest Capesize haul, so withdrawn Brazilian tonnage cuts tonne-miles by more than the tonnage alone. Horizon is Quarter rather than Regime because the duration of the shutdown was not knowable on the date.

EventName: Fire at the Cape Lambert A iron ore terminal
Rationale: Damage to a Rio Tinto shiploader at Cape Lambert A constrains Pilbara export capacity ahead of the cyclone season, and compounds with EV028.

EventName: Vale announces decommissioning of all upstream tailings dams
Rationale: Following the 2019-01-25 Brumadinho failure, Vale halts roughly 40 Mtpa of iron ore capacity. Announced after Brazilian market hours.

EventName: Vale reports cumulative suspensions of about 92.8 Mtpa
Rationale: Brucutu, Timbopeba and Alegria add to the January total, roughly doubling the withdrawn volume. A separate information event from EV026.

EventName: Cyclone Veronica halts Pilbara iron ore loading
Rationale: Near-stationary off the Pilbara coast for about 24 hours on 23 and 24 March, closing the Australian export ports. Coincides with the Brazilian suspensions, so both Capesize origins are constrained at once. Window is the cyclone's; port closure dates are not publicly archived.

EventName: Rio Tinto declares force majeure on Pilbara shipments
Rationale: Cyclone damage to Cape Lambert A converts the weather event into a contractual volume reduction. Guidance was cut on 2019-04-01 and cut again in the Q1 production report on 2019-04-16.

EventName: Indonesia bans coal exports
Rationale: Full export ban for January to protect domestic power supply, relaxed 2022-01-12 for producers meeting their domestic obligation and reopened from 2022-02-01. Removes Panamax and Supramax cargoes, while diverted buyers source from Australia and Colombia on longer hauls.

EventName: Black Sea Grain Initiative signed
Rationale: Restores Ukrainian grain exports, adding Handysize and Supramax cargoes on short hauls that partly displace the longer replacement voyages buyers had arranged from Australia and the Americas.

EventName: Russia withdraws from the Black Sea Grain Initiative
Rationale: Ukrainian grain again leaves by longer routes or by rail and river, which reduces cargo volume while lengthening what remains.

EventName: Simandou ships its first iron ore
Rationale: A new West African Capesize origin at a longer haul to China than either Australia or Brazil, adding tonne-mile demand against a fixed fleet as volumes ramp.

EventName: Ever Given blocks the Suez Canal
Rationale: Six-day closure delays transits and briefly tightens available tonnage, too short to move period rates.

EventName: Ever Given blocks the Suez Canal
Rationale: Same mechanism and the same brevity. Most dry bulk long-haul routes do not transit Suez, so the exposure is smaller but not nil.

EventName: Panama Canal restricts daily transits for drought
Rationale: Advisory A-48-2023 schedules cuts from 32 to 18 slots per day. The canal reversed course from 2024-01-16 and 18 never took effect; capacity normalised around August 2024. Diverted voyages lengthen, against queueing and auction costs falling on Panamax operators.

EventName: Panama Canal restricts daily transits for drought
Rationale: Same diversion mechanism, with little crude exposure since VLCCs do not transit the canal.

EventName: Tankers attacked in the Gulf of Oman
Rationale: Attacks on the Front Altair and Kokuka Courageous reprice Hormuz war-risk insurance, which raises the all-in cost of a Gulf voyage and is passed into freight.

EventName: OFAC sanctions COSCO Shipping Tanker (Dalian)
Rationale: Designation under E.O. 13846 removes a large VLCC operator from the compliant charter market at once, tightening available tonnage against unchanged cargo demand. Sanctions on the parent entity were lifted 2020-01-31.

EventName: Russia invades Ukraine
Rationale: Russian crude reroutes from short Baltic to Europe voyages toward India and China, lengthening average haul on an effectively fixed fleet. Tonne-mile demand rises without a vessel being added.

EventName: Russia invades Ukraine
Rationale: Europe substitutes seaborne coal for Russian pipeline gas, which adds long-haul thermal coal cargoes, against the loss of Ukrainian grain exports and higher bunker cost.

EventName: EU seaborne crude import ban and G7 price cap take effect
Rationale: Council Regulation (EU) 2022/879 Article 3m. Formalises the rerouting and splits the fleet into compliant and shadow tonnage, tightening the compliant pool that listed owners trade in.

EventName: EU refined products ban and product price caps take effect
Rationale: Extends the same haul lengthening to the products trades.

EventName: Houthi forces seize the Galaxy Leader
Rationale: First seizure of a merchant vessel in the southern Red Sea, beginning the risk repricing of Bab al-Mandab transits.

EventName: Houthi forces seize the Galaxy Leader
Rationale: Same corridor, but bulk carriers largely continued transiting into 2024, so the rerouting benefit did not accrue equally.

EventName: Maersk suspends Red Sea transits
Rationale: First major operator suspension. BP followed on 2023-12-18 and Operation Prosperity Guardian was announced on 2023-12-19. Cape of Good Hope routing adds roughly ten days per Asia to Europe voyage, absorbing tonnage and tightening effective supply.

EventName: Maersk suspends Red Sea transits
Rationale: Bulk carriers continued transiting in large numbers, so the tonne-mile gain is partial. The True Confidence attack on 2024-03-06 shows the risk was real without the rerouting being universal.

EventName: Israel-Iran conflict raises the Hormuz risk premium
Rationale: War-risk insurance on Gulf transits reprices sharply during the exchange. Roughly a fifth of seaborne crude passes Hormuz, so the premium enters the freight rate on most VLCC voyages.

EventName: OFAC designates Rosneft and Lukoil
Rationale: Largest Russian oil designations to that date. Compliant charterers withdraw from a further slice of Russian barrels, pushing cargo onto shadow tonnage and tightening the compliant fleet listed owners trade in.

EventName: MEPC 70 confirms the 2020 sulphur cap start date
Rationale: Resolution MEPC.280(70) fixes 2020-01-01 for the 0.50 percent limit. This is the information event; the 2020 entry into force was a formality by then.

EventName: MEPC 70 confirms the 2020 sulphur cap start date
Rationale: Same decision, with less scrubber uptake expected across the older bulk fleet.

EventName: IMO 2020 sulphur cap enters into force
Rationale: Compliance date for the limit confirmed at MEPC 70 in 2016. Timeline marker; the repricing belongs to EV045.

EventName: IMO 2020 sulphur cap enters into force
Rationale: Same reasoning.

EventName: MEPC 75 approves draft EEXI and CII amendments
Rationale: The information event for the efficiency regime. Speed and power constraints reduce effective supply, against an incentive to order replacement tonnage, which adds supply. Adopted at MEPC 76 on 2021-06-17, in force 2022-11-01, applying from 2023-01-01.

EventName: MEPC 75 approves draft EEXI and CII amendments
Rationale: Same mechanism, biting harder on an older and less efficient fleet, and the newbuilding response is correspondingly larger.

EventName: EU Emissions Trading System extended to maritime
Rationale: Allowance surrender on ships of 5,000 GT and above, phasing in from 40 percent of 2024 emissions. Legislated in 2023, so the date carried no news, and owners recover the cost through ETS surcharges and charterer-pays clauses.

EventName: EU Emissions Trading System extended to maritime
Rationale: Same obligation and the same pass-through.

EventName: Ballast water D-2 compliance deadline for all existing ships
Rationale: Deadline fixed since the convention entered into force in 2017, so nothing was learned on the date. The expected scrapping response did not appear: 2024 recycling fell to its lowest level since 2005.

EventName: Ballast water D-2 compliance deadline for all existing ships
Rationale: Same reasoning. Bulker demolition fell in 2024 rather than rising.

EventName: FuelEU Maritime applies
Rationale: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 sets declining greenhouse gas intensity limits on energy used at EU ports. Adopted September 2023, so the application date carried no new information, and the cost is contractually passed through.

EventName: FuelEU Maritime applies
Rationale: Same reasoning.

EventName: USTR Section 301 port fees on Chinese-built and operated vessels
Rationale: Announced 2025-04-17 with a zero fee window to 2025-10-13, in force from 2025-10-14 at 50 USD per net ton for Chinese operators and 18 USD per net ton for Chinese-built vessels, rising annually, then SUSPENDED for one year effective 2025-11-10. The regime therefore applied for about four weeks. Raises cost for owners of Chinese-built tonnage and advantages the rest, but only within that window.

EventName: USTR Section 301 port fees on Chinese-built and operated vessels
Rationale: Same split and the same four-week window, more material because a larger share of the bulk fleet is Chinese-built. China's mirrored fee on US-linked vessels took effect 2025-10-14 and was suspended in parallel.

EventName: IMO Net-Zero Framework adjourned for twelve months
Rationale: Removes near-term compliance cost while extending uncertainty over future fuel and newbuild decisions.

EventName: IMO Net-Zero Framework adjourned for twelve months

DataQualityFlag: The largest continuity break in the dataset. A NOK 129.5 distribution against a share trading in the NOK 100s makes the close-to-close move almost entirely a capital return. Falls after the 2025-09-25 validity window, so it does not enter the model. Yahoo's own adjustment was missing here and under-applied by about 9x on 72 of the 73 dividends; the 2020.OL file was rebuilt from Close and a frozen dividend snapshot (cumulative factor 1.2324x vendor, 2.2581x rebuilt), and this event is excluded rather than adjusted.

EventName: Diana Shipping bids for Genco and withdraws
Rationale: Proposal at USD 20.60 on 2025-11-24, hostile all-cash tender at USD 23.50 launched 2026-05-04, raised to USD 24.80, expired 2026-07-27 with 29.7 percent of the float tendered, withdrawn 2026-08-14. An all-cash offer is not an intra-basket transfer: Diana would fund it externally, so cash would enter one holding from outside while the other bears the financing. Diana was much the smaller of the two by market capitalisation, so the equal-weighted effect is asymmetric. No completion, so treating this as a deal would be wrong.

Rationale: Binding agreement to acquire AHTS AS for about USD 406m, with a private placement priced at USD 0.299 per share and a planned rename. The listing ceases to be a dry bulk company.

Rationale: USD 1.15bn in cash for the Saverys' low-carbon shipping arm, funded from the Frontline VLCC proceeds, plus USD 2.496bn of rolled-over debt and newbuilding commitments. The company is buying its way out of being a crude tanker pure play, which diversifies the earnings stream and takes on a large capex overhang at the same time. Rationale: Approved at the special general meeting on 2024-02-07 and closed the following day. Offshore wind crew transfer, container and chemical exposure enter a security that had carried none.
DataQualityFlag: THE BUSINESS BOUNDARY. From this date CMBT.BR is no longer a pure crude tanker security by vessel count, so returns after it are not comparable with the tanker lineage. The ticker change on 2024-07-15 and the name change on 2024-10-01 are labels applied to a shift that happened here. Crude remained the majority by tonnage until the Golden Ocean merger at EV081.

Rationale: Quarterly fleet disclosure: 10 VLCCs and 18 Suezmaxes against 17 Bocimar Newcastlemaxes, 56 Windcat crew transfer vessels, 5 Bochem chemical tankers and 4 Delphis container ships. Recorded as the evidence behind the EV116 boundary rather than as an event in itself.
DataQualityFlag: By mid-2026 the Euronav division held 4 VLCCs and 15 Suezmaxes out of about 203 vessels on the water, roughly 9 percent. CMB.TECH publishes no segment revenue and no deadweight, so any crude share used in this project has to be built from vessel counts and assumed class sizes, and the assumption stated.

EventName: The 2007 and 2008 orderbook delivers into a collapsed market
Rationale: Vessels ordered at the top of the cycle deliver on two to three year lead times regardless of demand, so fleet growth ran well ahead of trade growth through this period. The dominant driver of the post-crisis depression, and structural rather than event-dated.

EventName: The 2007 and 2008 orderbook delivers into a collapsed market
Rationale: Same lead-time mechanism on the tanker orderbook, with deliveries landing into falling cargo volumes.

EventName: VLCC ordering accelerates during the 2015 rate boom
Rationale: High spot earnings pull forward newbuilding orders that deliver on a two to three year lag, so the supply response to 2015 lands in 2017 and 2018. The mechanism is the lag itself: good rates today create tonnage later.

EventName: Scrubber retrofits remove tonnage from service
Rationale: Vessels in the yard for exhaust gas cleaning installation ahead of the sulphur cap are out of the trading fleet, tightening effective supply while cargo demand is unchanged.

EventName: Scrubber retrofits remove tonnage from service
Rationale: Same mechanism with lower uptake across the bulk fleet, so a smaller share of tonnage is withdrawn.

EventName: Stored crude returns to market as the contango unwinds
Rationale: Floating storage releases both the cargo and the vessel at once: stored barrels displace fresh liftings while the tonnage that held them re-enters the spot market. Supply and demand move against the owner simultaneously, which is why the unwind is worse than the build was good.

EventName: Port congestion absorbs fleet capacity
Rationale: Quarantine protocols, crew change restrictions and terminal backlogs hold vessels at anchor, removing effective capacity without removing a single ship from the fleet. The dominant supply-side driver of the 2021 dry bulk market.

EventName: Port congestion absorbs fleet capacity
Rationale: Same mechanism, materially weaker because tanker terminals were less congested than bulk and container berths.

EventName: The bulker orderbook falls to a multi-decade low as a share of fleet
Rationale: Fuel technology uncertainty and constrained shipyard capacity suppress ordering, so future fleet growth is capped years ahead regardless of what rates do. The mirror of EV110: weak ordering today creates scarcity later. Structural, with no single announcement date.
